properties.address: 1 W Register St, Edinburgh EH2 2AA, UK

properties.foundation_analysis: Bedrock comprises Carboniferous sedimentary strata of the Inverclyde and Strathclyde Groups, predominantly calciferous sandstones interbedded with siltstone and basaltic volcanic intrusions. Primary structural lithics consist of fine-to-medium-grained Craigleith and Hailes pale buff-to-grey quartz-arenite sandstones. Subterranean hydrological run-off drains south-west toward the palaeo-lacustrine basin of the drained Nor' Loch. Mortars are historic hot-mixed, non-hydraulic lime and sand matrices with localized Portland cement repointing on mid-to-late 20th-century infills.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Perimeter and interior parkland planting consists of mature *Platanus × acerifolia* (London plane), *Acer pseudoplatanus* (sycamore), *Tilia cordata* (small-leaved lime), and *Betula pendula* (silver birch). Late-September phenology: dense, mature canopies exhibiting early autumn senescent chlorosis, fading from deep olive green to muted ochre and pale yellow along outer leaf margins, with intact foliage volume and visible branch frameworks beneath.

properties.architectural_summary: Central public garden square centered on the 1821 Melville Monument: a fluted Roman Doric sandstone column atop a multi-tiered rusticated ashlar pedestal, surmounted by a heroic stone figure. Perimeter block layout features Georgian classical townhouses (4 to 5 storeys), Victorian commercial palazzi, and late-20th-century corporate office blocks (5 to 7 storeys). Rectified orthogonal geometry: plumb vertical masonry walls, straight cornices, rusticated ashlar basements, vertical timber 6-over-6 and 2-over-2 sash-and-case fenestration grids, modern flat-panel curtain-wall glazing, and mansard slate roofs with lead-dressed dormers.
